title: Trigonometric identities, equations, and applications
purpose: Transform trigonometric expressions with valid reasoning and find complete solutions rather than a single calculator answer.

lessons.title: Identities and domain-aware simplification
lessons.objective: Verify an identity through valid transformations on its common domain and identify invalid proof steps.
lessons.coverage: Reciprocal, quotient, and Pythagorean identities; rewriting in sine/cosine; factoring; common denominators; and the distinction between identity and equation.
lessons.activity: Choose a justified next step in a proof, track excluded angles, and test a counterexample to a proposed nonidentity.
families: Complete a short identity proof with justified steps
Find the first invalid step or missing domain restriction
lessons.generatorRules: Use reviewed transformation paths rather than unrestricted generated proofs. Numerical agreement at sample points is supporting evidence, not proof of an identity.
lessons.commonError: Assuming the desired identity at an intermediate step, canceling terms across addition, or erasing exclusions.
lessons.feedback: Return to the last justified expression, name the relevant identity, and state its required nonzero denominators.
lessons.checkpoint: A reciprocal rewrite, a Pythagorean simplification, a proof-step choice, and a domain condition.

lessons.title: Angle sums and double angles
lessons.objective: Use sum, difference, and double-angle identities to evaluate exact expressions and explain invalid distributive shortcuts.
lessons.coverage: Sine/cosine sum and difference identities, tangent denominator restrictions, double-angle forms, and choice of a form that matches available information.
lessons.activity: Compare sin(a+b) with sin(a)+sin(b), then complete a correct derivation using a supplied identity and known exact values.
families: Evaluate nonstandard exact angles by decomposition
Compute a double-angle value from a ratio and quadrant or select an equivalent identity
lessons.generatorRules: Choose angles built from reviewed special-angle combinations. Include quadrant information when recovering a missing sign. Half-angle and product-to-sum work stays optional.
lessons.commonError: Distributing sine over addition, using the wrong sign in cosine sums, or choosing the wrong square-root branch.
lessons.feedback: Use a simple counterexample, then reconstruct the correct formula with signs attached to each term.
lessons.checkpoint: Exact sum, exact difference, double-angle calculation, and identity selection.

lessons.title: Complete trigonometric solution sets
lessons.objective: Find every solution on a stated interval and express general periodic families when requested.
lessons.coverage: Factoring, substitution with sine/cosine, zero-product reasoning, multiple-angle arguments, periodic families, endpoints, and risks of dividing by a trig factor.
lessons.activity: Place all predicted solutions in an ordered list, compare them with graph intersections, and identify the root lost by dividing by sin(theta).
families: Solve a basic or factored trig equation on a finite interval
Express general solutions and detect omitted periodic branches
lessons.generatorRules: Specify angle units and interval inclusion explicitly; generate a known complete root set and deduplicate equal boundary values. Include equations with no solutions.
lessons.commonError: Returning only the principal inverse value, losing a factor-zero solution, or adding an excluded endpoint.
lessons.feedback: Separate factor branches, identify each period, and list candidate angles before filtering the interval.
lessons.checkpoint: A basic equation, a factored equation, a multiple-angle interval problem, and a general-solution form.

lessons.title: Non-right triangles and model ambiguity
lessons.objective: Choose the law of sines or cosines, solve a non-right triangle, and identify whether supplied measurements permit zero, one, or two triangles.
lessons.coverage: Side-angle correspondence, included-angle cases, triangle angle sum, triangle inequalities, the ambiguous side-side-angle case, and interpreting a geometric result.
lessons.activity: Enter side and angle measurements, predict the number of possible triangles, then inspect each valid solution using a diagram and text table.
families: Solve a valid side-angle-side or side-side-side triangle
Classify and solve ambiguous side-side-angle measurements
lessons.generatorRules: Construct valid cases from known triangles and deliberately include impossible and two-solution cases. Reject zero-area triangles and state rounding tolerance only after exact relationships are used.
lessons.commonError: Pairing an angle with an adjacent side in the sine law, forgetting the second sine solution, or accepting impossible lengths.
lessons.feedback: Label opposite pairs, test angle sums, and verify the proposed sides against a second relationship.
lessons.checkpoint: Method choice, cosine-law calculation, sine-law calculation, and ambiguity classification.

anchor.answer: Factor sin(x)*(2*sin(x)-1)=0. The complete set is {0, pi/6, 5*pi/6, pi}. The right endpoint 2*pi is excluded.

moduleExit: The quiz must include a lost-root trap and a domain-sensitive identity; a single inverse-trig calculator result is insufficient for an interval equation.
